pt.r: O Parque Provincial dos Dinossauros é um parque provincial em Alberta, no Canadá. Tem 80,9 km² e está protegido desde 1955, sob gestão do governo provincial. Na classificação da IUCN, é uma reserva natural estrita: a prioridade é a pesquisa científica e a visitação é muito restrita.
pt.h: Criado em 27 de junho de 1955, no jubileu de 50 anos de Alberta, para proteger os leitos de fósseis do vale do rio Red Deer. Em 1979 virou Patrimônio Mundial da UNESCO, pelos badlands e pela importância internacional dos fósseis.
pt.ff: Um dos depósitos de dinossauros mais ricos do mundo: 58 espécies de dinossauros já foram descobertas ali, e mais de 500 exemplares estão em museus pelo planeta. O conjunto fóssil soma quase 500 espécies, de esporos de samambaia a grandes carnívoros. O vale guarda também matas ciliares ao longo do rio.

en.r: Dinosaur Provincial Park is a provincial park in Alberta, Canada. It covers 80.9 km² and has been protected since 1955. It is managed by the provincial government. Under the IUCN system it is a strict nature reserve: science comes first and visits are tightly restricted.
en.h: Established on 27 June 1955, Alberta's 50th jubilee year, to protect the fossil beds of the Red Deer River valley. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979 for its badlands and the international importance of its fossils.
en.ff: One of the richest dinosaur fossil sites in the world: 58 dinosaur species have been found here, and more than 500 specimens are in museums around the globe. The fossil assemblage includes nearly 500 species, from fern spores to large carnivores. The valley also holds riverside woodland.

es.h: Creado el 27 de junio de 1955, en el jubileo de 50 años de Alberta, para proteger los yacimientos fósiles del valle del río Red Deer. En 1979 fue declarado Patrimonio Mundial de la UNESCO por sus badlands y por la importancia internacional de sus fósiles.
es.ff: Uno de los yacimientos de dinosaurios más ricos del mundo: allí se han descubierto 58 especies de dinosaurios, y más de 500 ejemplares están en museos de todo el planeta. El conjunto fósil suma casi 500 especies, desde esporas de helechos hasta grandes carnívoros. El valle conserva además bosques de ribera.

en.r: The largest national park in Alberta's Rocky Mountains, north of Banff and west of Edmonton. A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984, with the glaciers of the Columbia Icefield, lakes, waterfalls and hot springs.
en.h: It began as Jasper Forest Park on 14 September 1907 and became a national park in 1930. The Grand Trunk Pacific railway arrived in 1911 and founded the town now called Jasper. In 1908 explorer Mary Schäffer reached Maligne Lake using a map drawn by Nakoda guide Samson Beaver.
en.ff: At least 50 mammal species, including moose, elk, bighorn sheep, mountain goats, grizzly bears and wolves.

en.r: In Alberta's southwest corner, where the Rockies meet the prairie, on the border with Montana's Glacier National Park. Together they form the Waterton-Glacier International Peace Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
en.h: Canada's fourth national park, it began in 1895 as the Kootenay Lakes Forest Reserve, at the suggestion of rancher Frederick Godsal. In 1932 it joined the neighbouring US park to form the world's first international peace park.
en.ff: More than 1,000 plant species, about 20 found nowhere else. Grizzly and black bears, bighorn sheep, mountain goats, elk, cougars and bison.

pt.r: Parque nacional que existiu de 1909 a 1940 perto de Wainwright, no centro-leste de Alberta, criado para salvar o bisão-das-planícies da extinção. Hoje a área é a base militar de Wainwright.
pt.h: Foi um dos "parques de regeneração" das pradarias canadenses, feitos para recuperar bisões e antilocapras. Fechou em 1940, saiu da lista em 1947 e as terras passaram ao Ministério da Defesa. O primeiro guarda-parque foi Bud Cotton, de 1912 a 1940.

en.r: A national park that existed from 1909 to 1940 near Wainwright, in east-central Alberta, created to save the plains bison from extinction. The land is now Canadian Forces Base Wainwright.
en.h: It was one of the prairie "regeneration parks" meant to restore bison and pronghorn. It closed in 1940, was delisted in 1947 and the land went to the Department of National Defence. Its first warden was Bud Cotton, from 1912 to 1940.
en.ff: Its focus was the plains bison, often called "buffalo". The recovery worked so well that the park became overcrowded.
at: Now a military area, not open as a park
The story continues at Elk Island and Wood Buffalo national parks

es.h: Fue uno de los "parques de regeneración" de las praderas canadienses, pensados para recuperar bisontes y berrendos. Cerró en 1940, salió de la lista en 1947 y las tierras pasaron al Ministerio de Defensa. Su primer guardaparque fue Bud Cotton, de 1912 a 1940.
es.ff: El foco era el bisonte de las llanuras, llamado "búfalo". La recuperación funcionó tan bien que el parque quedó superpoblado.
at: Hoy es zona militar, sin visitas como parque
La historia sigue en los parques nacionales Elk Island y Wood Buffalo

pt.r: A 35 km de Edmonton, em Alberta, é o maior parque nacional do Canadá totalmente cercado. Teve papel decisivo na salvação do bisão-das-planícies.
pt.h: A região de Beaver Hills abrigou por séculos manadas de uapitis, bisões e alces, e há mais de 200 sítios de acampamentos indígenas. O parque nasceu como reserva de uapitis e virou parque nacional em 1913; bisões criados ali repovoaram outras áreas do Canadá e dos EUA.
pt.ff: Tem a maior densidade de grandes herbívoros do Canadá: bisões-das-planícies e bisões-da-floresta, uapitis, alces e veados. Abriga também o maior e o menor mamífero terrestre da América do Norte, o bisão-da-floresta e o musaranho-pigmeu. Mais de 250 espécies de aves.

en.r: 35 km from Edmonton, Alberta, it is Canada's largest fully fenced national park. It played a key role in saving the plains bison.
en.h: The Beaver Hills sheltered herds of elk, bison and moose for centuries, and there are over 200 Indigenous campsite remains. The park began as an elk reserve and became a national park in 1913; bison raised here restocked other areas of Canada and the US.
en.ff: It has Canada's highest density of hoofed mammals: plains and wood bison, elk, moose and deer. It also hosts North America's largest and smallest land mammals, the wood bison and the pygmy shrew. More than 250 bird species.
at: Roadside bison viewing

es.ff: Tiene la mayor densidad de grandes herbívoros de Canadá: bisontes de llanura y de bosque, uapitíes, alces y ciervos. Alberga además el mayor y el menor mamífero terrestre de América del Norte, el bisonte de bosque y la musaraña pigmea. Más de 250 especies de aves.

en.r: Dry Island Buffalo Jump Provincial Park is a provincial park in Alberta, Canada. It covers 34.5 km² and has been protected since 1970. It is managed by the provincial government. en.r: Big Knife Provincial Park is a provincial park in Alberta, Canada. It covers 3 km² and has been protected since 1962. It is managed by the provincial government. Under the IUCN system it is category II, the national park category: it protects whole ecosystems and welcomes visitors.
en.h: Named after Big Knife Creek. By tradition, a Cree man called Big Man and a Blackfoot warrior called Knife fought to the death here. In the early 1900s the area was a hideout for cattle rustlers and home to One-Eyed Jack Nelson, who made moonshine; remains of his cabin and stills survive. The park was established in 1962 and fully opened in 1972.
en.ff: Summer birds include yellow-bellied sapsucker, spotted towhee, eastern phoebe and turkey vulture; year-round residents include bald eagle, black-capped chickadee and ruffed grouse. Mammals include elk, moose and porcupines.

en.r: A former national park north of Medicine Hat, in southeastern Alberta, created in 1922 to protect pronghorn, which were nearly extinct. It closed in 1938 and was delisted in 1947.

en.ff: Its focus was the pronghorn, North America's fastest land mammal.
at: Now a military area (Suffield)
